author: wittjosiah
principle: When refactoring a typed API, do not widen its generic constraints, return type, or parameter type to something less precise than what is achievable (e.g. `any`, a broad supertype, or a dropped generic parameter) -- preserve or restore the original precision.
fix_shape: Restore the narrower/generic type signature instead of the widened one.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Name a namespace import after the module it comes from; do not rename it (e.g. with a suffix like `Ns`) to dodge a naming collision or a lint rule.
fix_shape: Import the namespace under its canonical module name and resolve the collision another way.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Do not add a type cast (`as any`, `as X`) to work around a type error -- fix the underlying type or add a runtime assertion so the value is actually verified.
fix_shape: Remove the cast and adjust the type/signature (or add a real runtime assertion) so no cast is needed.

principle: A type-guard/instance-check function's accepted input type should match the scope implied by its name -- reject related-but-different kinds even at the type level rather than silently accepting them.
fix_shape: Narrow the accepted type (or add an explicit rejecting overload) so the function only accepts the kind it is named for.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Do not paper over a design problem with elaborate conditional/utility types (chained `Omit`s, conditional types) -- fix the underlying type shape so the manipulation is not needed.
fix_shape: Restructure the source type so the derived props type does not need to omit brand/derived fields.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Do not perform side effects (registering a callback, mutating shared state) at module load time -- wire dependencies explicitly through an initialization call.
fix_shape: Move the registration/callback wiring into an explicit init function invoked by the composition root, not top-level module code.

author: dmaretskyi
principle: Define an overloaded public function as `export const foo: { (...): ...; (...): ...; } = impl`, not the `function foo(...)` declaration-overload syntax.
fix_shape: Rewrite the function as a const with a type-literal listing each overload, assigned an implementation.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Do not modify a file as part of a refactor unless the change is actually required by it -- avoid unnecessary churn.
fix_shape: Revert the unrelated/unneeded edits in that file.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Do not cast to silence the type checker -- use a runtime assertion/narrowing function so the value is actually verified before use.
fix_shape: Replace the `as`/`as any` cast with a call to an assertion helper (e.g. `Type.assertObject`).

author: wittjosiah
principle: Derive an instance's type from the schema-provided helper (e.g. `Type.InstanceType<...>`) rather than hand-declaring the shape again.
fix_shape: Use the canonical derived-type helper instead of re-authoring an equivalent interface by hand.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Provide one unified accessor for deriving a value instead of scattering ad hoc branching logic (`instanceof` checks, etc.) at each call site.
fix_shape: Add/use a single shared accessor function and call it everywhere the value is needed.

author: wittjosiah
principle: When a generic API cannot infer a specific result type, it should fall back to an explicit safe type (e.g. an `Unknown` entity type), not let inference silently decay to `any`.
fix_shape: Add an explicit fallback overload/type so unresolved cases type as the safe fallback instead of `any`.

author: wittjosiah
principle: A mutation-callback API's draft parameter should already carry a mutable type -- do not make callers re-cast it to a mutable type inside the callback.
fix_shape: Type the update/mutate callback's draft parameter as mutable at the source so callers need no cast.

author: wittjosiah
principle: Do not call an `Option`/try-style function and then immediately force-unwrap the result with `!` -- call the throwing/direct variant if failure is not actually handled.
fix_shape: Replace `tryParse(...)!` with the direct/throwing `parse(...)` call.
